case.title: The young star nobody classified
case.hook: Listed as a 'suspected variable' for decades. Gaia, ZTF and NEOWISE agree: a young star in Perseus whose own disk keeps blotting it out.
case.summary: NSV 1302 surfaced from Oddsky hunt H-0001 as the only unexplained survivor of 22,125 Gaia-selected fading Sun-like stars. It is a known young star in Per OB2; its data show an irregular disk-occultation 'dipper': 1.2 mag swings in ZTF, chromatic Gaia dips, and a warm infrared excess. A modest result, recorded honestly.

claims.text: Found by Oddsky hunt H-0001 (Gaia-selected fading Sun-like stars) as one of 18 stars with Gaia dips deeper than 0.8 mag on 2+ transits, and the only one of them not already catalogued as an eclipsing binary, a blend, or a variable of known type.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: ZTF g (450 points, 2018-2025) varies irregularly by 1.2 mag (2nd-98th percentile) about a 13.26 median, with no long-term trend (0.004 mag/yr) and no significant period between 1 and 60 days (top power 0.05).
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: On Gaia transits BP and RP dim together, dBP/dRP = 1.32 with r = 0.98: chromatic, as dust is, but greyer than interstellar dust, which hints at large grains.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: NEOWISE W1-W2 = 0.43 (median of 21 visits): a strong excess from warm dust, as an inner disk produces.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: TESS shows 'dips' of 0.7-2.5 mag lasting only 1-3 hours in two sectors. Disk occultations last longer than that; these are treated as probable systematics until checked against target pixels.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: SIMBAD lists the star only as a generic star ('*'). It appears in a 2015 WISE census of young stellar objects in Per OB2 and in membership lists of young Perseus groups, but no SIMBAD-indexed paper describes its dimming.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: A young star in Per OB2 whose inner disk intermittently blocks it (an irregular 'dipper').
hypotheses.would_falsify: A strict period (spots or an eclipsing companion), or no infrared excess.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: Spots on a young, active star.
hypotheses.would_falsify: Spots give periodic, low-amplitude (<0.3 mag) modulation; ZTF shows no period and 1.2 mag swings.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.would_falsify: Gaia and ZTF independently show chromatic dimming; only the TESS hour-long dips are suspect.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

query.adql: SELECT source_id, ra, dec, parallax, parallax_over_error, pmra, pmdec, ruwe, phot_g_mean_mag, phot_bp_mean_mag, phot_rp_mean_mag, bp_rp, phot_variable_flag, teff_gspphot, distance_gspphot, non_single_star, DISTANCE(POINT(56.92895976487,35.01226990153), POINT(ra,dec))*3600 AS sep_arcsec FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE 1=CONTAINS(POINT(ra,dec), CIRCLE(56.92895976487,35.01226990153,0.008333333333333333)) ORDER BY sep_arcsec
